metadata.title: IND Submissions for Individualized Antisense Oligonucleotide Drug Products: Administrative and Procedural Recommendations Guidance for Sponsor-Investigators: Draft Guidance for Sponsor-Investigators

candidates.statement: The focus of this guidance is on administrative and procedural aspects of interacting with FDA 26 on development programs for individualized ASO drug products, such as the approach to 27 obtaining feedback from FDA and the expectations and process for making regulatory 28 submissions to FDA. The guidance provides high-level recommendations about informed 29 consent and the requirement for institutional review board (IRB) review of protocols for trials of 30 individualized ASO drug products. This guidance also addresses the initial development of these 31 individualized ASO drug products; it does not address regulatory considerations for the 32 development of these drug products for marketing and continued, long-term treatment of patients 33 with the disease for which the drug product is being developed. This guidance also does not 34 address the nonclinical data, the clinical data, or the product quality requirements that must be 35 met to initiate administration of these individualized ASO drug products in humans. 36
candidates.context: This guidance is intended for sponsor-investigators 2 (hereafter referred to as sponsors) 17 developing individualized investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) drug products for a 18 severely debilitating or life-threatening genetic disease. 3 Most often, individuals with such 19 diseases will not have FDA-approved treatment options and their diseases will be rapidly 20 progressing, resulting in early death and/or devastating irreversible morbidity within a short time 21 frame. In these situations, drug development targeted at a larger number of patients with the 22 ASO is not anticipated because of the specificity of the mechanism of action of the ASO drug 23 product combined with the rarity of the treatment-amenable patient population. 24 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Office of New Drug Policy in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the Food and Drug Adminis

candidates.statement: Although the guidance is intended to help sponsors seeking to develop an individualized ASO 38 drug product, the principles and practices outlined in the guidance may also be applicable to 39 developing other types of individualized drug products (i.e., non-ASO). Sponsors who consider 40 applying the principles outlined in this guidance for non-ASO individualized drug products 41 should first consult with the appropriate review division. 42
candidates.context: 3 Severely debilitating means diseases or conditions that cause major irreversible morbidity. Life-threatening means diseases or conditions where the likelihood of death is high unless the course of the disease is interrupted and those with potentially fatal outcomes, where the endpoint of clinical trial analysis is survival (see 21 CFR 312.81). In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 44 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 45 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 46 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 47 not required. 48

candidates.statement: Complete and well-organized submissions, in a format conducive to scientific review, can help 150 increase the efficiency of FDA’s review and prevent delays in FDA responses to requests for 151 information. All IND submissions should include overall summaries with enough detail to allow 152 FDA staff to understand the regulatory and developmental context of the submission. 153

candidates.statement: Under FDA’s IND regulations at 21 CFR 312.23(b), a sponsor ordinarily is not required to 161 resubmit information previously submitted to FDA but instead may incorporate the information 162 by reference. If the information is in an existing IND application, the sponsor should identify the 163 IND number, type of submission in which the information is located (e.g., nonclinical 164 information amendment), the date of submission, page number(s), and, if applicable, volume 165 number. If a sponsor seeks to reference information submitted to the Agency by a person other 166 than the sponsor, the sponsor should include a written statement authorizing such reference that 167 is signed by the person who submitted the information. However, in either instance, depending 168 on when the information was submitted and its format (e.g., paper versus electronic), voluntarily 169 resubmitting the information may facilitate and expedite FDA’s review. 170
candidates.context: electronic submission to facilitate and expedite review of the submissions. Electronic 157 submissions for research INDs are not required to be in electronic Common Technical Document 158 (eCTD) format; however, they may be voluntarily submitted in that format. 9

candidates.statement: The package should include information to justify the proposal to develop an individualized 181 ASO drug product. Generally, the content of a pre-IND meeting package should also include 182 information to support proof of concept, initial dosing in humans, and safety monitoring plans 183 for initial human dosing, as well as the proposed clinical protocol. Furthermore, the package 184 should include the nonclinical, bioinformatic (information related to the design of the 185 oligonucleotide), and product quality data that the sponsor intends to submit with its IND. 186

The content of a meeting package, including for pre-IND meetings, should be organized 190 according to the proposed meeting agenda. 10 The package should be a sequentially paginated 191 document with a table of contents, appropriate indices, appendices, and cross references. 192

candidates.statement: When the sponsor has gathered the recommended information, the sponsor should submit a 201 research IND to FDA. To aid FDA in understanding the proposed development context and 202 related benefit-risk considerations, the sponsor should include in the initial IND submission the 203 justification for developing an individualized ASO drug product. During the pre-IND meeting, 204 or at some other point before submitting the IND, the sponsor should discuss expectations for the 205 content of the IND submission with the relevant FDA review division, since some of the content 206 and format requirements at 21 CFR 312.23 may not be relevant for this type of application. 207

Sponsors should provide a complete report for each in vitro and in vivo study intended to 217 characterize the pharmacological activity and the safety of the investigational drug. Each study 218 report should include, but not be limited to, the following: 219
candidates.context: Because the proposed study will be first in humans, it is unlikely that human data will be 211 available at the time of the initial IND submission. Thus, only product manufacturing and quality 212 information, bioinformatic (information related to the design of the oligonucleotide), and 213 nonclinical data will support the safety of initiating administration to a participant. It is critical 214 that the nonclinical data be adequately presented and documented. 215 • A statement of the purpose of the study 221

candidates.statement: Because of the nontraditional nature of drug development in this arena, complex ethical issues 286 may arise. As such, sponsors should consider conferring with a medical ethicist when 287 developing their protocol. 288
candidates.context: D. Ethical and Human Subject Protection Considerations 284

candidates.statement: Under FDA regulations, a protocol under which an individualized ASO drug product is 292 administered to a human subject must be reviewed by an IRB (21 CFR Part 56), which must 293 fully evaluate the protocol and ensure that risks to the subject are reasonable in relation to the 294 anticipated benefits (21 CFR 56.111(a)(2)). The IRB should be provided with the results of all 295 relevant nonclinical safety studies in animals that have been conducted. Sponsors should 296 consider contacting their IRB as early as possible. If the ASO drug product will be administered 297 to a child, the IRB must ensure that the protocol complies with the requirements under 21 CFR 298 part 50, subpart D. 299

Under FDA regulations, informed consent must be obtained under circumstances that provide 303 prospective participants, or their legally authorized representatives, sufficient opportunity to 304 consider whether to participate and that minimize the possibility of coercion or undue influence 305 (21 CFR 50.20). The sponsor should include a copy of the informed consent document in the 306 original IND submission. 307
candidates.context: The informed consent document and the consent discussion should appropriately emphasize in a 309 clear manner that the ASO drug product is experimental, the reality that the benefit is uncertain 310 and the potential risks are unknown, and that additional costs to the participant may be associated 311 with the administration of the drug product. When appropriate, the consent document and 312 consent discussion should include information that the administration of the ASO drug product 313 will be the first use in humans of the investigational drug and relevant information from 314 nonclinical safety studies in animals that have been conducted that could potentially inform the 315 safety of the participant. 316
